- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 5–10 days.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply downward bias of 3–5% for 3–7 days post-spike.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive days falling >1.5% from peak), model overestimates continuation; adjust downward by 1–3% for next 7–14 days.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price declines, model often underestimates drop; increase forecast downward by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate early in the horizon (first 7–10 days) when sentiment is neutral or positive; apply downward correction of 1–2% for first 7 days.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust; apply downward correction of 2–4% for next 5–10 days.
- In low-sentiment environments (sentiment <0.33 for 5+ days), model underestimates downside risk; add 1–3% downward bias for next 7–14 days.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–3% for next 3–5 days unless sentiment is strong positive.
- If true outcome shows strong downward trend (e.g., 3+ consecutive days falling >2% from prior), model often fails to recognize trend; apply downward bias of 2–4% for next 7–14 days.
